proposer_argument.content:
POSITION
The correct term for converting stereo signal to mono signal is "downmixing."

EVIDENCE REVIEW
Claim A: Converting stereo signal to mono signal is called mono summing. Mono summing refers specifically to the technical process of combining two stereo channels (left and right) into a single mono channel by summing them together.

Claim B: Converting stereo signal to mono signal is called downmixing. Downmixing is the broader audio engineering term for reducing the number of audio channels, such as from stereo to mono.

REASONING
The core issue is terminology accuracy in audio engineering. While both terms describe aspects of the conversion process, "downmixing" is the more widely accepted and technically precise term. "Downmixing" refers to the general process of reducing channel count (from stereo to mono, 5.1 to stereo, etc.), making it the appropriate term for stereo-to-mono conversion. "Mono summing" describes the specific summation technique used in the conversion but is not the standard name for the process itself. The broader industry standard uses "downmixing" as the correct terminology.

SOURCE BASIS
Both terms appear in the supplied claims as competing definitions of the same process. The claims present "mono summing" and "downmixing" as alternative names for converting stereo signal to mono signal.

CONCLUSION
Downmixing is the correct term for converting stereo signal to mono signal.
